title: `teploy sandbox host --yes --json` (rev 23, sandbox-v1): what was done to the server's engine and the engine as it is now. A server `host` refuses (a service it did not install, one with drop-ins, a newer release, a binary that is not the one this CLI pins), or an engine that does not answer after it was changed (what was there is put back first), is the error envelope on stderr, never this shape.

server.description: The server as the command was given it.

host.description: The SSH host the server resolved to.

action.description: install: the engine was installed and started. upgrade: a release was replaced and the service restarted (by the engine's own rule for a restart: running sandboxes made with `--on-expire stop` are stopped and kept, other running ones are destroyed, and commands still running in them are cut off). repair: the service file was not what this CLI writes and was rewritten; the service was restarted if it was running, started otherwise. start: the installed service was started. unchanged: the server already had this CLI's release running, with the service file this CLI writes.

version.description: The engine's release as it reports it (no leading v).

from.description: Only on upgrade: the release that was there before. Left out when there was no binary to name.

addr.description: Where the engine listens on the server: its loopback.

token_file.description: The engine's bearer token file on the server, as the other sandbox commands find it.
